description: Learn an operation for a website nobody has shared yet, in one call: use it after find_sites found no site or no operation for what the user asked. Give the https page URL on a public host that shows the answer, with {param} placeholders (trigger: https://site.com/search?q={q}), the user's own values (args), and two other real values of the same kind that you pick (args2, args3: other searches, other ids, other places the site has). When the catalog already has an operation for the same page on that domain (one search words do not find while it is unconfirmed), it calls that with args instead and answers with `reused`: no browser, nothing learned; fresh: true learns the page anyway. Otherwise it loads the page in a browser with args and with args2, picks the data request and the fields, and checks the result with args3 and with a replay that sends no cookies. The answer to the user's request is in `data`; `signature` is the new operation, callable from then on with call_operation. `chosen` is the request and recipe it used, and `alternatives` the other candidates: if data is not what the user wanted, call learn_site again with the same args, `captures` from the result (no browser), and pickRequest and/or a recipe (extract and pick for JSON, html or embedded for a page). A list behind a 'Show more' or next-page button: pass steps that click it, so each run loads page 2. The list is then learned with its paging when both runs show it (paging in the result), and data comes with nextPage and hasMore; pass paging to say it yourself (the cursor param is the op's own, never in args). Sharing with the catalog is automatic for a public read when the user turned sharing on; if they never answered whether to share, it asks them once (or `next` tells you to ask). An operation that needed a login is shared only with the user's yes. Only reads: a write is learned with the CLI. On failure follow `next` once (nextCall is the same step as data).

args.description: the user's own values, by param name: their answer comes back in data

args2.description: another real value of the same kind, chosen by you: it becomes the shared example

args3.description: a third real value, different from both: the check that the operation works

captures.description: an earlier result's captures: learn again from them, with no browser

embedded.description: a regex for JSON inside the page; group 1 marks where it starts

extract.description: a path into a JSON answer: data.items, sections[*].items

fresh.description: learn the page anew, not calling an op someone shared for it: when a reused answer is not what the user wanted

html.description: a list in the page: {"items":"<css>","fields":{"name":"<css>[@attr]"},"empty":"<css>"}; empty: the element a page with no results shows instead of the list

intent.description: what the operation is for, in general words (it is shared): 'search books by title'

op.description: a camelCase operation name, e.g. searchBooks; default: from the URL path

paging.description: how the list pages, when the automatic pick is wrong: param takes the next page, next is the path in the whole answer to its value (path~regex keeps group 1 of a string there, e.g. a next-page URL). Without next, the pages are numbered: put param in args, args2 and args3

pick.description: fields kept per item; name=path renames

pickRequest.description: a request id from chosen or alternatives

site.description: site name; default: the trigger's host

steps.description: UI steps after the page loads, {param} filled: [{"action":"click","selector":"#more"}] loads page 2 of a list. Actions: click, fill, press, wait (ms), goto (value)

trigger.description: the page URL with {param} placeholders, e.g. https://site.com/search?q={q}

write.description: not supported: writes are learned with the CLI

name: learn_site
